title: The band's peak, Herschel's death, movies and hit records
summary: He thinks the band peaked about 1941, recalls Herschel Evans's death, Hollywood pictures, and records such as 'Sent for You Yesterday'.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Well when do you reckon the band was at its peak?
Yes, we were getting better ensemble.
But I mean Herschel had gone by then hadn't he? When did Herschel go?
Herschel left in either '38 or '39. (Herschel Evans died in February, 1939---Ed.)

Yes, we had Lester and Buddy Tate was no Herschel was gone because Buddy was out in California. And then we'd shoot down to Los Angeles and make a picture. We made a couple of pictures and we were making these little, little movies that you put a quarter in. But we did quite a few movies, you know. Hit Parade of 1942 or something like that. Reveille at Beverley. Those, that we made.
And records were going pretty well?
Yes, records were going very nicely. Some of the best records was started off with a, Jimmy Rushing singing the blues Christmas time and I want to see Santa Claus, those kind of blues.
Well 'Sent for you Yesterday' that was the big, the first big record wasn't it?

Right. 'Goin' to Chicago', And then after that we started getting or even before that we had had some numbers that, band numbers that were beginning to 'Miss Thing' and things that Basie used to write. Taps Miller, 'The
World is Mad', 'Down for Double' and 'Digging for Dex and 'Pandussie Stomo and all those things.
